newsitem.title: CHINA: Eastern Communications buys back 15 mln B shares.
newsitem.headline: Eastern Communications buys back 15 mln B shares.

text.p: Shares of communication equipment maker Eastern Communications fell sharply on Friday after it announced it had bought back 15 million B shares from the secondary market.
After the announcement, the stock was the worst performer on the Shanghai B share market, falling $0.040 or 5.26 percent to $0.720, on volume of 376,000 shares.
It made the announcement in the Shanghai Securities News, saying it planned to distribute the stock to shareholders as part of a private placement.

Eastern Communications bought the 15 million shares before September 9 at a price just below the initial offer price of $0.8, said a broker with China Guotai Securities, the company's main underwriter.
The company's stock issue in July was greatly oversubscribed.
According to China's securities regulations, a company which has its shares oversubscribed can issue shares equal to 15 percent of the original amount, which Eastern Communications did.

But, since the company's shares were listed in August, they have been trading for most of the time under the issue price of $0.80 mainly due to overall weak market conditions on the Shanghai's B share market.
Brokers said that the company bought the 15 million shares to stabilise the share price and prevent the underwriters from having to buy large amounts of shares.
